The main takeaway from our work is that

a left ventricular hypertrophy threshold of greater than or equal 50% above normative values is a good predictor of a decreased coronary flow reserve in the absence of significant coronary artery obstruction.
a left ventricular hypertrophy threshold exists above which coronary vasodilatory reserve is predictably impaired.
left ventricular mass is an important predictor of coronary flow reserve in patients without coronary artery disease, and this is true regardless of whether LV mass is indexed by BSA or by height.
